title: Entry processing preserves free variables
statement: Fix $n$ variables and consider the entry-processing step of the Razborov decoding procedure, which takes a term $t$ (a conjunction of literals) over these variables, a natural number $w$, two restrictions $\sigma, \rho_0 \colon \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Option}\,\mathrm{Bool}$, and a list $\mathit{aux}$ of pairs $(\mathbb{N} \times \mathrm{Bool})$, and returns a restriction as the first component of its output. If $\sigma$ leaves a variable $v$ free (that is, $\sigma(v) = \mathtt{none}$), then the restriction produced by this step also leaves $v$ free.
hypotheses_covered: σ leaves v free (σ v = none)
caveat: The routine razborovDecode.processEntries is not among the supplied definitions and is an opaque internal step of the decoder, so its actual behaviour (and the roles of t, w, ρ₀, and aux) cannot be described mathematically; only its input/output signature and the single genuine hypothesis σ v = none can be rendered faithfully.
replaced:
If $\sigma\,v = \mathrm{none}$, then the decoder's \texttt{processEntries} routine leaves
$v$ unset; the resulting $\sigma$ is still $\mathrm{none}$ at $v$.
